The best-known example is Justice Dalveer Bhandari of India. Your question doesn't name a country, so I'm assuming you mean India.
He served as a senior judge of the Supreme Court of India for about seven years, then resigned in 2012.[1]
The UN Security Council elected him on 27 April 2012 to fill a vacancy on the ICJ.[2] The vacancy came from the resignation of Judge Awn Shawkat Al-Khasawneh of Jordan.
In 2017 the UN General Assembly re-elected him for a nine-year term beginning 6 February 2018.[3] That term is due to expire in early February 2027.
Other Indian jurists have also served on the ICJ. Raghunandan Swarup Pathak, then Chief Justice of India, served on the ICJ during 1989–91.[4] Nagendra Singh and Benegal Narsing Rau also served on it. I'm adding those two from memory, so please verify them.
If you meant a judge from another country's Supreme Court, tell me which one and I'll look it up.
